newsitem.title: CHINA: Canada offers C$75 million credit line to China.
newsitem.headline: Canada offers C$75 million credit line to China.

text.p: Canada intends to negotiate the extension of up to C$75 million in new concessional credit to China, Minister for International Trade Art Eggleton said on Tuesday.
"Canada is committed to supporting Canadian businesses in China," he told the Canada-China Business Council (CCBC), holding its annual general meeting in Shanghai.
"The extension of a concessional line of credit will ensure that Canadian exporters are on the same footing as competitors who use similar financial facilities in China," he said.
The Export Development Corporation (EDC) has been asked to begin discussions with Chinese officials on this concessional line of financing, he said.

The C$75 million will be in addition to existing lines of credit with Chinese banks, which can provide up to C$430 million in export financing to support the sale of Canadian goods and services, Eggleton said.
China is Canada's fourth largest export market, he said.
Eggleton witnessed the signing of 11 agreements worth C$96 million between Canadian and Chinese organisations on Tuesday, the CCBC said in a statement.
These include six contracts valued at C$79 million and eight agreements in principle, such as memoranda of understanding, valued at C$17 million, it said.
The biggest, worth C$40.7 million, was between Westcoast Energy International of Vancouver and Shanghai Number 1 Iron & Steel Group to build, operate and transfer a 50-megawatt power plant, it said.
Westcoast will be project manager and plant operator for the first 15 years of the 20-year joint venture contract, with the Chinese party purchasing the power from the plant, it said.
Eggleton said he would visit Beijing in December at the invitation of his Chinese counterpart, Wu Yi.
"This will be my first opportunity to conduct a full review of our bilateral economic and trade relationship since becoming minister for international trade," he said.

Separately on Tuesday, the Atomic Energy of Canada Ltd and China National Nuclear Corporation signed a contract for construction of two 700-megawatt CANDU-6 nuclear reactors worth C$4.0 billion, Canadian officials said.
China's Premier Li Peng and Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien witnessed the signing ceremony at a hotel in a suburb of Shanghai, they said.
